column17: Genel Energy is a London-listed independent oil and gas company with primary assets in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, including production-sharing interests at Taq Taq and Tawke fields. The company has operated in Iraqi Kurdistan since the early 2000s under contracts with the Kurdistan Regional Government. Genel remains one of the leading independent operators active in the KRI upstream sector.

column17: BP operates in Iraq primarily through the Rumaila Operating Organisation (ROO), a joint venture with Basra Oil Company and CNPC to develop the Rumaila super-giant field, one of the world's largest oil fields. BP holds a 38% technical service contractor interest and has been active on the field since 2009. Rumaila produces well over one million barrels per day.

TotalEnergies holds interests in the Halfaya field in Missan Governorate and signed a landmark integrated energy deal with the Iraqi government in 2021 covering Artawi field development, solar power generation, seawater treatment, and gas capture across Basra. The French major is one of the largest foreign investors in Iraq's current energy transition projects. TotalEnergies' Iraq portfolio spans both upstream oil and clean energy infrastructure.

column17: SLB (formerly Schlumberger) operates extensively across Iraq's major oilfields, providing drilling, reservoir characterization, and production services. The company has a significant presence in southern Iraq's prolific Basra region and works with both national and international operators. SLB is among the largest oilfield services providers active in Iraq.

column17: Lukoil, Russia's largest privately-owned oil company, holds the operator stake in the West Qurna-2 field in southern Iraq, one of the world's largest undeveloped oil accumulations. Lukoil signed its service contract with Iraq's Ministry of Oil in 2009 and commenced production in 2014. The company serves as technical service contractor alongside Iraqi state partners.

column17: Weatherford International provides drilling, well evaluation, and production services in Iraq, supporting IOC-operated and national company projects across multiple governorates. The company supplies well construction, artificial lift, and completion equipment solutions. Weatherford has maintained a continuous operational base in Iraq to serve the country's expanding upstream sector.

Halliburton has maintained operations in Iraq since the post-2003 period, offering well completion, cementing, stimulation, and drilling services to operators across Iraqi oilfields. The company supports major upstream projects in Basra and other producing regions. Halliburton is one of the three largest oilfield services companies active in the country.

Iraq National Oil Company (INOC) is the state-owned holding entity re-established in 2018 to oversee Iraq's oil and gas sector and coordinate the regional operating companies. INOC manages Iraq's hydrocarbon policy and acts as the umbrella above Basra Oil Company, North Oil Company, and other subsidiaries. It is the apex institution of Iraq's upstream petroleum industry.

column17: China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) is one of the most active international oil companies in Iraq, holding stakes in Rumaila (38%), Halfaya (37.5%), Missan fields cluster, and Ahdab. CNPC's engagement in Iraq dates to the 1990s and expanded substantially after 2009 under technical service contracts. The company is widely regarded as Iraq's largest foreign upstream investor by barrels managed.

Basra Oil Company (BOC) was established to replace the South Oil Company and manages production from the supergiant Rumaila, West Qurna 1, West Qurna 2, Majnoon, and Zubair fields. It is among the world's highest-volume oil producers and operates in partnership with BP, Lukoil, Shell, and ExxonMobil. BOC is the single most important entity in Iraq's oil export infrastructure.

North Oil Company (NOC) manages hydrocarbon extraction in northern Iraq, primarily the historic Kirkuk oil field whose production dates to the 1930s. Established in 1972 after nationalization of the Iraq Petroleum Company, NOC has been a cornerstone of Iraq's oil industry for decades. The company operates in disputed territories straddling Arab and Kurdish regions.

Missan Oil Company is a state-owned Iraqi enterprise responsible for the Missan oil fields cluster in southeastern Iraq, including Buzurgan, Abu Ghirab, and Fauqi fields. The company partnered with CNPC and CNOOC under a technical service contract signed in 2009. Missan's fields have seen significant capacity growth through Chinese investment and technology transfer.

Midland Oil Company (MOC) is an Iraqi state oil company overseeing central Iraq fields including the Ahdab field developed under contract with CNPC. The company manages assets in Wasit Governorate and surrounding areas and reports directly to Iraq's Ministry of Oil. MOC plays a key role in unlocking Iraq's central-region reserves.

Dhi Qar Oil Company manages oil production in Dhi Qar governorate in southern Iraq, including the Nasiriyah field and surrounding blocks. The company is state-owned and operates under the Iraqi Ministry of Oil. Development of the Nasiriyah block has attracted sustained international interest given its significant proven reserves.
